gen-dafont-fenwick-fs-epilogue: Graceful and bookish, Fenwick keeps every curve at a constant width while Epilogue loosens up beneath it with a springy, wire-thin line. One does literary polish; the other, friendly modern ease.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-bespoke-serif: Franchise stands tall and narrow, its letters jammed shoulder to shoulder. Bespoke Serif, a classic serif with hairlines about half the weight of its stems, gives it a dignified, moderate-height counterweight if you give the heading the larger size.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-sentient: Sentient brings a pinched, closed-in sophistication to the text. Over a long passage its crossbars, a touch thinner than the stems, keep a classic serif feel, while Franchise's wide-tipped c shapes stay a tall, tight shout above.
gen-dafont-galette-fs-merriweather-sans: Galette's horizontals match its verticals exactly, giving the serif heading a flat, understated authority. Merriweather Sans carries a longer read in sturdy, tall-bodied words, its e opening clearly to the right, with only slight contrast in the strokes.
gen-dafont-gobold-fs-sentient: Sentient reads sophisticated and contemporary, its apertures pinched shut and its crossbars slightly lighter than the stems. Sentient against Gobold's open, widely spaced curves is the strongest thing here: one closed and tight, the other airy and wide.
gen-dafont-good-times-poppins: Good Times opens wide with a clear-gapped e and lowercase thick as bundled cable, a restrained round-brush swell. And Poppins, a sans of rope-loose curves, earns its place beside it, though the heading really earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-halogen-fs-recia: Sleek as bent steel rod, Halogen has no hairline anywhere against its stems. Recia, a text serif, has a soft, ink-drawn modulation and generous openings, so one is the sharper headline and the other the warmer read.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-paquito: Stretched sideways and marker-plain, Helsinki looks calm and tall in the lowercase. But shrink it down and its plainness fades, while Paquito, a text serif, would feel crowded if you made it large.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-supreme: Helsinki stretches its lines sideways, every stroke the same width from stem to curve. And Supreme gives a longer passage a thick, dense band through the middle, with letters held open instead of curled shut.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-trench-slab: Helsinki looks stretched sideways, drawn with steady marker pressure from the first letter to the last. But Trench Slab, a text serif, is where a dignified, refined feel lives, with its low gap between x-height and caps.
